entries.title: Kampagne und Skirmish
compact_lines: Kampagne fuehrt mit eigenem Stand durch die Einfuehrung.
Skirmish nutzt dein frei bearbeitetes Team; Multiplayer oeffnet Host/Join.
detail_lines: Teameditor und Teambibliothek gehoeren zu Skirmish. Eine neue Kampagne veraendert dieses Team nicht.
Fortsetzen laedt einen sicheren Basis-Meilenstein. Ein vorhandener Kampagnenstand wird nur nach Bestaetigung ersetzt.

entries.title: Team Identity
compact_lines: Name and emblem describe this saved team.
They do not change mission truth or NPC stats.
detail_lines: Use this area to label the local roster before starting play.
Character names, portraits and values are edited on the selected NPC sheet.

entries.title: Team Name
compact_lines: Name of this saved rookie team.
Changing it does not alter NPC stats or mission state.
detail_lines: The name is stored with the local roster save and is used for menu and staging readability.

entries.title: Team Symbol
compact_lines: Small image used to recognize this team in menus.
It is visual identity, not a hidden bonus.
detail_lines: The symbol is chosen from existing project images and saved with the roster editor data.

entries.title: Team Focus Points
compact_lines: These are team focus points, not NPC skill points.
Raising one focus rebalances points from the other unlocked focuses.
detail_lines: The 30 point rookie cap keeps a created team from starting overpowered.
A five point increase lowers the five other unlocked focus values by one each when they can move.
NPC values are changed on the character sheet.

entries.title: Tactics Focus
compact_lines: Tactics favors leaders and cleaner command execution.
It is a team focus, not one NPC value.
detail_lines: This focus is meant to bias rookie generation toward coordination.
Edit Leadership directly on a character when you want a specific NPC changed.

entries.title: Medical Focus
compact_lines: Medical favors recovery, medics and safer casualty handling.
It does not spend points on one NPC.
detail_lines: Use it as a team-level rookie identity and balancing knob.
Individual medic quality still comes from the character's visible values.

entries.title: Engineering Focus
compact_lines: Engineering favors repairs, doors, generators and objectives.
It shapes team identity before individual edits.
detail_lines: This focus is for generator and balancing rules on the saved team.
A specific engineer still needs direct character values in the sheet.

entries.title: Piloting Focus
compact_lines: Piloting favors dropship, freighter and fighter skill.
Platform skills are visible in the character sheet.
detail_lines: Good dropship pilots combine Dropship Piloting, Awareness and Discipline.
Freighter and Fighter Piloting are separate platform values.

entries.title: Discipline Focus
compact_lines: Discipline favors formation, pressure control and buddy behavior.
It is separate from per-NPC Discipline edits.
detail_lines: Use this focus to keep a rookie team calmer in its overall identity.
The individual Discipline row still controls one character directly.

entries.title: Recon Focus
compact_lines: Recon favors awareness, recognition, stealth and scouts.
It is a saved team-level focus.
detail_lines: This focus helps describe and later bias rookie team creation.
Use individual Awareness, Recognition and Stealth rows for one NPC.

entries.title: Focus Lock
compact_lines: Locks one team focus value while you rebalance the others.
It affects editor input only, not mission simulation.
detail_lines: Locked focus bars ignore mouse, plus/minus and slider changes until unlocked.
Locked rows are skipped when another focus pulls or returns points.
The lock is stored with the team editor data so the budget row stays predictable while editing.

entries.title: Context Help Mode
compact_lines: Controls whether short help popups appear on hover or focus.
Off, compact and expanded modes change presentation only.
detail_lines: This setting must not alter commands, loadouts, character values or mission simulation state.

entries.title: Fog of War
compact_lines: Changes how much hidden map information the mission view reveals.
Uses the existing FoW contract instead of storing UI-side truth.
detail_lines: Mode names and visibility behavior must match the fog-of-war contracts and runtime resolver.

entries.title: Help Mode
compact_lines: Toggles help inspection for the current screen.
It is a UI overlay control and does not issue gameplay commands.
detail_lines: In off mode it may open a short overview, but hover popups stay disabled until settings change.

entries.title: Roster
compact_lines: Shows available crew and their current assignment state.
Selecting a character updates detail panels without duplicating roster truth.
detail_lines: Roster data comes from the player roster store and meta profile builder.

entries.title: Transfer Team
compact_lines: Stages crew for movement toward the FOB or mission chain.
A staged card is not final mission truth until the transfer flow confirms it.
detail_lines: The help must stay read-only because transfer state belongs to the existing meta flow.

entries.title: Fireteams
compact_lines: Builds Homebase fireteams and shows each member loadout inline.
These controls edit staging data, not simulation runtime truth.
detail_lines: Member dropdowns write the same loadout state used by #13 and mission export.

entries.title: Loadout
compact_lines: Detail editor for the focused fireteam loadout.
The same armor and weapon choices also appear compactly in #10.
detail_lines: The panel shares member loadout state with Homebase fireteam cards and export payloads.

entries.title: Flightdeck
compact_lines: Boards fireteams onto the selected dropship from Homebase.
Shipcards accept fireteam drops when their craft can stage.
detail_lines: Boarding uses the existing direct staging payload and does not create a second dropship state.

entries.title: Character Popup
compact_lines: Opens the focused character sheet outside the numbered windows.
Use it for inspection while keeping #10, #13 and Flightdeck visible.
detail_lines: The popup renders the shared two-column sheet and remains read-only in Homebase.

entries.title: Fireteams
compact_lines: Groups crew into squads for mission staging.
Selection changes the focused team view, not the SimulationRoot directly.
detail_lines: Mission handoff preserves stable unit IDs and fireteam order for later setup.

entries.title: Flightdeck
compact_lines: Shows available transport craft and boarding status.
Boarding buttons call existing FOB callbacks only.
detail_lines: Visual craft cards and pads are presentation; vehicle truth stays in transport state.
Damaged or lost air assets show repair/replacement ETA and stay unavailable until recovery completes.

entries.title: Loadout Weight
compact_lines: Shows combined armor and weapon weight for this loadout.
No Weapon adds zero weapon weight.
detail_lines: Weight is calculated by LoadoutModifierResolver from armor and WeaponData weights.

entries.title: Core Values
compact_lines: Main 0.00 to 1.00 values used by character and mission systems.
In the team editor, bars can be dragged or changed with plus/minus.
detail_lines: Core rows come from MetaUnitProfile skill_values and character-bundle derivation.
Edits write back through the roster editor; mission runtime does not read UI state as truth.

entries.title: Group Budget
compact_lines: Shows the point budget for one editable value group.
Raising one unlocked bar can pull points from other unlocked bars.
detail_lines: One 0.05 step equals one editor point in the visible budget row.
Lowering a value frees points into the budget.
Locked bars keep their current value; if there are not enough movable points, the dragged bar snaps back to its maximum affordable value.

entries.title: Value Lock
compact_lines: Locks this one character value during budget edits.
The visible value remains unchanged until unlocked.
detail_lines: Use this before lowering or raising nearby values when you want this exact row preserved.
The lock is stored in the team editor data and does not create gameplay authority.

entries.title: Command Matrix
compact_lines: Issues tactical orders through existing command controllers.
The HUD never writes mission state as its own truth.
detail_lines: Detailed help can name command modes after the command-mode contract exists.

entries.title: Mission Control
compact_lines: Shows mission phase, route and high-level control state.
Controls must stay reachable while help is visible.
detail_lines: Help positioning should avoid active command buttons when another side has room.

entries.title: Height Tool
compact_lines: Edits terrain height while preserving surface and object fields.
Slopes and cliffs follow the terrain hill rules contract.
detail_lines: Height authoring must roundtrip through map save/load without changing gameplay fields.

entries.title: Save and Load
compact_lines: Stores the authored map and loads it back for editor or mission use.
Map transfer to multiplayer keeps manifest consent explicit.
detail_lines: Help may reference file identity and manifest checks, but must not auto-accept downloads.

entries.title: Tactical Profiles
compact_lines: Sets enemy tactic, heavy role, air-asset risk and comms for the scenario.
These fields save into mission data and stay out of UI gameplay truth.
detail_lines: Anti-armor threat requires a valid AT weapon such as rocket launcher or rail gun.
Air-risk profiles are scenario authoring hints; runtime still resolves damage through SimulationRoot.

entries.title: Host or Join
compact_lines: Starts or joins a lobby before gameplay state exists.
Ready and mission start remain server-authoritative.
detail_lines: Lobby help may explain map consent and roster ownership without bypassing session checks.

entries.title: Character Updates
compact_lines: Shows mission results that were applied to roster progression.
Returning to meta screens keeps the same character IDs.
detail_lines: Debrief help must not apply XP, morale or frustration by itself.

entries.title: Identity
compact_lines: Name, portrait and callsign identify the same roster unit across screens.
Changing focus must not create a new character record.
detail_lines: Identity values come from MetaUnitProfile and roster generation or saved roster data.

entries.title: Character Name
compact_lines: Roster display name for this NPC.
Editing it changes identity text, not stats or role.
detail_lines: The name stays attached to the same stable unit ID across Homebase, FOB and Mission views.

entries.title: Portrait
compact_lines: Visual portrait used for this NPC's cards and sheets.
It helps recognition but does not affect gameplay values.
detail_lines: Portrait changes use the existing portrait catalog and keep the same character record.

entries.title: Role and Loadout
compact_lines: Shows role, fireteam and the currently staged equipment summary.
Loadout text is read from the active profile or FOB member loadout.
detail_lines: The sheet displays loadout state; weapon and weight rules stay in WeaponData and the resolver.

entries.title: Role
compact_lines: Primary job label for reading the character quickly.
Role can influence badges and suggested duties, not direct UI truth.
detail_lines: Role labels are built from roster identity and character-bundle derivation.

entries.title: Role Category
compact_lines: Broad roster grouping used for scanability and assignment hints.
It is not a hidden stat and does not replace skill values.
detail_lines: Category comes from MetaUnitProfile roster_role_category when present.

entries.title: Fireteam
compact_lines: Shows the current fireteam assignment or UNASSIGNED.
Moving the character between teams changes staging, not sheet-local state.
detail_lines: Fireteam text is supplied by Homebase or FOB context and preserves stable unit IDs.

entries.title: Badges
compact_lines: Small badges summarize derived role fit from the current profile values.
Grey badges show reachable fits that are not strong enough yet.
detail_lines: Badges are derived by NPCRankBadgeResolver from core values, communication, behavior, platform values and small loadout context.
Hover a single badge for the exact score source and threshold formula.

entries.title: Shooter Badge
compact_lines: Shooter comes mainly from Accuracy, Awareness, Recognition and weapon context.
It explains fighting fit, not a locked class.
detail_lines: The current threshold is 0.52 and the score blends Accuracy, Awareness, Recognition, Discipline and Order Fidelity.
Rifle, SMG and sniper loadouts are context bonuses, not a separate class truth.

entries.title: Leader Badge
compact_lines: Leader comes mainly from Leadership, Speech Quality, Order Fidelity and Autonomy.
Use it when choosing Fireteam Leaders.
detail_lines: The current threshold is 0.52 and the fireteam lead flag is only a small context bonus.
Raise Leadership, Speech Quality, Recognition, Discipline, Order Fidelity or Autonomy.

entries.title: Pilot Badge
compact_lines: Pilot comes from platform value plus calm situational and communication values.
Dropship, freighter, fighter and vehicle handling are checked.
detail_lines: The current threshold is 0.52 and the best platform value is blended with Awareness and Discipline.
Speech Quality, Contact Stability and Initiative also matter for flight fit.

entries.title: Medic Badge
compact_lines: Medic comes from Discipline, Recognition, Speech Quality and Stability.
Medictool and old role text are only context bonuses.
detail_lines: The current threshold is 0.52 and the score also reads Awareness, Order Fidelity and Contact Stability.

entries.title: Heavy Badge
compact_lines: Heavy comes from Toughness, Contact Stability, Discipline and Accuracy.
It marks heavier fighting equipment.
detail_lines: The current threshold is 0.52; rail gun, rocket launcher, panzerfaust and heavy armor are context bonuses.

entries.title: Engineer Badge
compact_lines: Engineer comes from Recognition, Discipline, Awareness and Order Fidelity.
It marks technical or repair fit.
detail_lines: The current threshold is 0.52; tech role words and engineer trait tags are only context bonuses.

entries.title: Enemy Badge
compact_lines: Enemy comes from team or faction context.
It is a readability tag for opposing units.
detail_lines: Team Bravo or enemy team_id can mark the unit as hostile.

entries.title: Traits
compact_lines: Traits are notable character tags from the roster profile.
They explain tendencies but are not free-form balance formulas.
detail_lines: Trait names come from UnitTrait data or stored trait tags on the profile.

entries.title: Trait: Aggressive
compact_lines: Aggressive favors accuracy but reduces toughness.
Expect a more forceful combat tendency.
detail_lines: Current UnitTrait modifiers: Accuracy +0.10 and Toughness -0.10 before derived summaries.

entries.title: Trait: Cautious
compact_lines: Cautious trades speed and accuracy for toughness.
Good for safer, less reckless profiles.
detail_lines: Current UnitTrait modifiers: Accuracy -0.05, Toughness +0.10 and Speed -0.10.

entries.title: Trait: Steady
compact_lines: Steady gives a small accuracy and speed lift.
Useful for reliable generalists.
detail_lines: Current UnitTrait modifiers: Accuracy +0.05 and Speed +0.05.

entries.title: Trait: Reckless
compact_lines: Reckless boosts speed but lowers toughness.
Fast profiles can become harder to keep safe.
detail_lines: Current UnitTrait modifiers: Speed +0.15 and Toughness -0.15.

entries.title: Trait: Calm
compact_lines: Calm improves leadership and accuracy.
Strong candidate trait for future fireteam leads.
detail_lines: Current UnitTrait modifiers: Leadership +0.15 and Accuracy +0.05.

entries.title: Status and Recovery
compact_lines: Shows availability, injury or recovery state for the character.
Recovery text is read from profile state and does not heal by itself.
detail_lines: Follow-up systems may make recovery actionable; the sheet remains read-only.

entries.title: Status
compact_lines: Current availability or screen-specific status text.
Use it to see whether the character is active, staged or recovering.
detail_lines: Status text is passed in by the owning screen and mirrors existing meta state.

entries.title: Recovery
compact_lines: Shows medbay or downtime state when the unit is not fully ready.
Remaining turns or days are display values from the profile.
detail_lines: The character sheet does not advance timers; recovery logic belongs to meta progression.

entries.title: Morale
compact_lines: Morale summarizes how well the character is holding up after missions.
Higher values are generally better for future team feel.
detail_lines: The number is stored in progression data; this help does not define final balance effects.

entries.title: Frustration
compact_lines: Frustration tracks pressure or bad mission experience.
Lower values are usually easier to manage.
detail_lines: The value is progression data and should be explained by future morale rules when finalized.

entries.title: Teamfit
compact_lines: Summarizes relationship fit with other roster members.
Use it as a staging hint, not as a hidden command override.
detail_lines: Teamfit text is built from relationship links and the roster relationship model.

entries.title: Best Fit
compact_lines: Shows the strongest positive known relationship link.
A good fit is a planning clue for future cohesion decisions.
detail_lines: Best Fit is summarized from relationship link affinity data when available.

entries.title: Tension
compact_lines: Shows the strongest negative known relationship link.
Use it to avoid rough team combinations when possible.
detail_lines: Tension is read from relationship link affinity data and is not recalculated in UI.

entries.title: Relationship Links
compact_lines: Lists a small set of known links to other roster members.
Longer relationship simulation remains outside this screen.
detail_lines: Links come from stored relationship data and are shortened for compact UI.

entries.title: Progress
compact_lines: Shows XP, mission history and recent team history.
Progress is applied by mission results, not by this panel.
detail_lines: Progress rows read from MetaUnitProfile progression and history arrays.

entries.title: XP
compact_lines: Experience gained from resolved mission outcomes.
Current help avoids promising a final leveling formula.
detail_lines: XP is stored in progression data after mission/debrief flow applies results.

entries.title: Missions
compact_lines: Count of completed or recorded missions for this character.
It helps separate rookies from veterans at a glance.
detail_lines: Mission count comes from progression data or mission history length.

entries.title: FTL Impact
compact_lines: Shows how a fireteam leader affects plan quality, communication and breakouts.
It summarizes tactical progression without exposing private history.
detail_lines: The value is derived from Leadership, Tactical Sense, Communication, Discipline, Initiative and Team Cohesion.
Mission outcomes can improve it slowly, while frustration or poor cohesion can slow progress.

entries.title: Accuracy
compact_lines: How reliable the character is with aimed combat tasks.
Used as a character value, not recalculated by the sheet.
detail_lines: Accuracy comes from skill_values and may feed combat effects through existing resolvers.

entries.title: Speed
compact_lines: How quickly the character tends to move or act.
Loadout weight can later modify movement through the resolver.
detail_lines: Speed is stored as a profile skill; movement modifiers come from existing loadout logic.

entries.title: Toughness
compact_lines: How well the character handles pressure and harm.
Shown as profile data, not as a new health formula.
detail_lines: Toughness can be used by combat and recovery systems through their own contracts.

entries.title: Awareness
compact_lines: How well the character notices battlefield context.
Useful for reading scouts, guards and overwatch roles.
detail_lines: Awareness is part of profile skill values and may feed perception-related resolvers.

entries.title: Recognition
compact_lines: How well the character identifies contacts and friend-or-foe cues.
It helps explain cautious or reliable combat reads.
detail_lines: Recognition comes from skill values and should follow perception contracts when expanded.

entries.title: Stealth
compact_lines: How quietly or subtly the character can operate.
Useful for scouts and concealed approaches.
detail_lines: Stealth is profile data and may affect concealment through existing mission rules.

entries.title: Discipline
compact_lines: How reliably the character follows orders under stress.
Higher discipline supports steadier behavior in planned actions.
detail_lines: Discipline is a profile value; command behavior effects belong to tactical resolvers.

entries.title: Leadership
compact_lines: How well the character supports team command and coordination.
It is useful when choosing fireteam leads.
detail_lines: Leadership comes from profile skills and feeds existing leader/teamfit derivation.

entries.title: Communication
compact_lines: Shows speech quality and quantity style values.
These values explain feedback tone, not direct mission truth.
detail_lines: Communication rows are read from MetaUnitProfile communication_values.

entries.title: Platform Skills
compact_lines: Vehicle and craft skills are derived from core values and behavior profile.
They help choose pilots, drivers or craft crew.
detail_lines: Platform rows read explicit platform_values; otherwise UnitProfileMath derives them from core, communication and behavior values.
Flightdeck assignment still reads saved roster data and does not accept UI-only truth.

entries.title: Derived Values
compact_lines: Summaries derived from methods, functions and specialties.
They help scan fit without replacing the detailed rows.
detail_lines: Derived text is built by the profile formatter and rank badge resolver.

entries.title: Behavior Profile
compact_lines: Behavior axes describe tendencies such as initiative and order fidelity.
They are hints for future tactical behavior, not UI commands.
detail_lines: Behavior rows come from profile behavior_axes and character-bundle derivation.

entries.title: Last Mission
compact_lines: Shows the latest recorded mission result for this character.
It is a history readout, not an active mission control.
detail_lines: Last mission text is read from the profile mission_history array.

entries.title: Fireteam History
compact_lines: Shows the latest known fireteam history entry.
It helps explain past assignment context.
detail_lines: History comes from MetaUnitProfile fireteam_history and is shortened for the sheet.

entries.title: Method Tags
compact_lines: Summarizes how this character tends to approach tasks.
Tags are scan hints and do not issue orders.
detail_lines: Method tags are formatted from method_scores or stored method summary text.

entries.title: Function Scores
compact_lines: Shows derived fit for functions such as scout or coordinator.
Use it as assignment guidance, not a hard class lock.
detail_lines: Function scores are built from profile function_scores and character-bundle derivation.
Overwatch reads Accuracy, Awareness, Discipline and Recognition.
Coordinator reads Leadership, Speech Quality, Recognition and Discipline.
Pilot functions read platform skill plus awareness, discipline, recognition or communication.

entries.title: Primary Specialty
compact_lines: Best readable specialty for this character.
It helps choose roles without hiding the underlying values.
detail_lines: Primary specialty is read from the profile or character bundle.

entries.title: Secondary Specialty
compact_lines: Secondary fit or backup specialty when one is known.
Empty values mean no strong secondary has been recorded.
detail_lines: Secondary specialty is display data from MetaUnitProfile.

entries.title: Speech Quality
compact_lines: How clear or useful the character's communication tends to be.
Useful for reading command feedback style.
detail_lines: Speech quality comes from profile communication_values.

entries.title: Speech Quantity
compact_lines: How often the character tends to communicate.
More speech is not always better; it describes style.
detail_lines: Speech quantity comes from profile communication_values.

entries.title: Initiative
compact_lines: Tendency to act without waiting for perfect certainty.
This describes behavior style, not a direct command.
detail_lines: Initiative is read from behavior_axes and may inform later behavior resolvers.

entries.title: Order Fidelity
compact_lines: How closely the character tends to follow assigned orders.
Useful when choosing steady fireteam members.
detail_lines: Order fidelity is read from behavior_axes and does not override commands in UI.

entries.title: Signature Control
compact_lines: Tendency to keep noise and exposure under control.
Helpful for stealth or careful movement reads.
detail_lines: Signature control is a behavior axis and not a separate visibility formula here.

entries.title: Contact Stability
compact_lines: How steady the character tends to be after contact.
Useful for reading pressure behavior.
detail_lines: Contact stability is read from behavior_axes and may support later tactical logic.

entries.title: Autonomy
compact_lines: How independently the character tends to operate.
High autonomy is a behavior tendency, not permission to ignore authority.
detail_lines: Autonomy comes from behavior_axes and must stay below command authority contracts.

entries.title: Ground Vehicle
compact_lines: Fit for operating ground vehicles.
Derived from speed, recognition, awareness, discipline and behavior axes.
detail_lines: Without override, ground vehicle handling derives from speed, recognition, awareness, discipline, initiative, stability and autonomy.

entries.title: Dropship Piloting
compact_lines: Fit for dropship pilot assignments.
Derived from flight-relevant core, communication and behavior values.
detail_lines: Without override, dropship piloting derives from awareness, recognition, discipline, speed, speech quality and order fidelity.
Stability and autonomy also affect the derived value.

entries.title: Freighter Piloting
compact_lines: Fit for freighter or cargo craft assignments.
Derived from steady transport and route-control values.
detail_lines: Without override, freighter piloting derives from toughness, recognition, discipline, speech quality and order fidelity.
Stability and autonomy also affect the derived value.

entries.title: Fighter Piloting
compact_lines: Fit for fighter craft assignments when those assets are used.
Derived from speed, accuracy, awareness and behavior axes.
detail_lines: Without override, fighter piloting derives from speed, accuracy, awareness, discipline, initiative and order fidelity.
Stability and autonomy also affect the derived value.

entries.title: Loadout Summary
compact_lines: Shows armor and both weapon slots for the focused character.
FOB member loadout overrides profile text when editing a team.
detail_lines: Weapon names are resolved through WeaponData; weight comes from LoadoutModifierResolver.

entries.title: Armor
compact_lines: Armor changes the carried loadout weight and protection intent.
Light, medium and heavy are the current playable armor choices.
detail_lines: Armor weight is resolved by LoadoutModifierResolver and not stored in the selector UI.

entries.title: Weapon Slot
compact_lines: Each member has two selectable gameplay weapon slots.
Visual-only attachment IDs are not selectable here.
detail_lines: Selections are normalized through WeaponData before mission setup receives them.

entries.title: SMG
compact_lines: Short-range attack weapon with light carried weight.
Good default when mobility matters.
detail_lines: SMG range, damage and weight come from WeaponData.

entries.title: Rifle
compact_lines: Balanced attack weapon for general combat range.
Use it when no specialist role is needed.
detail_lines: Rifle stats are read from WeaponData and may map to an existing visual loadout.

entries.title: Sniper
compact_lines: Longer-range attack weapon with higher carried weight.
Better for overwatch-style roles than close pushes.
detail_lines: Sniper range and weight are resolved from WeaponData.

entries.title: Rocket
compact_lines: Heavy attack weapon with high carried weight.
Use it when anti-armor or heavy impact is worth slower loadout.
detail_lines: Rocket weight and attack classification come from WeaponData and the resolver.

entries.title: Medictool
compact_lines: Support item for medic roles, not an attack weapon.
It is lighter than regular weapons.
detail_lines: Medictool is non-attack in WeaponData; healing rules stay in medic support logic.

entries.title: No Weapon
compact_lines: Leaves the slot empty and adds zero weapon weight.
A character may carry no attack weapon if both slots are empty.
detail_lines: None is normalized by WeaponData and produces no hidden fallback weapon.

entries.title: LMG
compact_lines: LMG is reserved for a future playable weapon entry.
It is not selectable until WeaponData defines gameplay stats.
detail_lines: Do not expose a visual-only heavy blaster as LMG without a WeaponData entry.

entries.title: Visual Only
compact_lines: Some weapon-looking assets are decorative attachments only.
They do not become selectable gameplay weapons by appearance.
detail_lines: Selectors must use WeaponData IDs, not visual_loadout IDs from the render mapping.

entries.title: Weapon Preview
compact_lines: Small image showing the selected weapon family.
Preview art is decorative and does not decide stats.
detail_lines: The preview path comes from WeaponData or FOB preview mapping and stays visual-only.

entries.title: Empty Slot
compact_lines: This slot has no weapon selected.
The preview is intentionally hidden.
detail_lines: An empty slot must not create a fallback rifle or hidden 3D weapon attachment.

entries.title: Unavailable Choice
compact_lines: A disabled choice is blocked because it is not a playable item here.
Visual-only assets need a real WeaponData entry before selection.
detail_lines: Disabled reasons should stay short and point to data boundaries, not hidden balance.

entries.title: Clear Loadout Focus
compact_lines: Clears the currently focused fireteam from loadout editing.
It does not delete the roster member or mission state.
detail_lines: The button only resets FOB loadout focus and leaves authoritative data paths intact.

entries.title: Member Loadout Row
compact_lines: Edits armor and two weapon slots for one fireteam member.
Each row keeps the member's stable unit ID.
detail_lines: Member rows update FOB member_loadouts, later handed to mission setup by unit ID.

entries.title: No Team Default
compact_lines: Armor and weapon choices are stored per member.
There is no hidden team-wide weapon default in this UI.
detail_lines: This keeps loadout handoff explicit for each unit before mission setup.

entries.title: Display Settings
compact_lines: Controls resolution, window mode and sync behavior.
Display settings change presentation only.
detail_lines: They must not alter simulation timing, mission commands or saved roster state.

entries.title: Audio Settings
compact_lines: Adjusts master, music and SFX volume.
The sliders feed the audio bus, not gameplay logic.
detail_lines: Combat and UI events emit audio requests; these values only scale playback volume.

entries.title: Input Reference
compact_lines: Shows current action prompts and common controls.
This panel is a reference, not a keybinding editor yet.
detail_lines: Changing command behavior still belongs to the command and input contracts.

entries.title: Gameplay Settings
compact_lines: Collects UI-facing gameplay options such as FoW and bubbles.
Settings describe modes; runtime systems still own truth.
detail_lines: Use this section to change presentation and feedback preferences before entering play.

entries.title: FoW Off
compact_lines: Reveals the mission map without hidden or unexplored masking.
Useful for debugging or open-information tests.
detail_lines: This mode should not create contacts or enemy knowledge by itself; it only changes visibility.

entries.title: Known Terrain FoW
compact_lines: Keeps the terrain readable while unit vision controls contact visibility.
Good default when learning the map.
detail_lines: Runtime vision still decides contacts; terrain remains visible so navigation context is not lost.

entries.title: Blackout FoW
compact_lines: Hides unexplored terrain until your units reveal it.
Use it for stricter reconnaissance play.
detail_lines: Known tiles and contacts still come from the FoW runtime, not from UI labels or help text.

entries.title: Host Lobby
compact_lines: Starts a local ENet lobby on the selected port.
The host owns mission start and authority checks.
detail_lines: Hosting creates session state only; gameplay truth begins later in SimulationRoot.

entries.title: Join Lobby
compact_lines: Connects to a host address and port.
Joined clients cannot bypass host authority.
detail_lines: The lobby records peer, roster and ready state before any mission commands are accepted.

entries.title: Ready State
compact_lines: Marks your peer ready or unready for mission start.
The host still decides when to start.
detail_lines: Ready state is lobby session data and must not mutate units, maps or combat state.

entries.title: Player Name
compact_lines: Name shown for this peer in the lobby.
Stored as lobby setup only.
detail_lines: It labels the peer assignment and does not create gameplay state.

entries.title: Player Roster
compact_lines: Selects which saved roster you bring.
Default multiplayer mode uses each player's local roster.
detail_lines: Only public roster preview data is shared.
Private progression and relationship data stay in the local player profile.

entries.title: Player Side
compact_lines: Chooses Alpha or Bravo for this peer.
Co-op keeps players together by default.
detail_lines: The host snapshot records the side before mission start assignments are built.

entries.title: Team Mode
compact_lines: Together means co-op on one side.
Versus allows opposing sides.
detail_lines: This is lobby configuration and is passed into the mission start assignment.

entries.title: Map Select
compact_lines: Host chooses the map for this lobby.
Clients can consent to unknown maps.
detail_lines: The map manifest contains id, hash and size so clients can detect mismatches.

entries.title: Connection Mode
compact_lines: LAN/VPN works inside reachable networks.
Direct Internet needs port forwarding or UPnP.
detail_lines: UPnP mode tries to open the host UDP port automatically on supported routers.
Two routers without forwarding, UPnP or VPN usually need a future relay.

entries.title: Start Mission
compact_lines: Host-only request to begin the mission with current lobby data.
Blocked when required consent or readiness is missing.
detail_lines: The session hands roster, map and peer assignments forward; clients do not start themselves.

entries.title: Leave Lobby
compact_lines: Disconnects from the current multiplayer session.
Back returns to the menu after the session is closed.
detail_lines: Leaving the lobby clears session state and does not fabricate mission results.

entries.title: Map Download Consent
compact_lines: Appears when the host offers a map your client does not have.
Accepting or rejecting is explicit.
detail_lines: Consent checks the map manifest and must not auto-accept unknown files.

entries.title: Roster Ownership
compact_lines: Shows whether the host roster or local roster is used.
Authority stays with the host/server contract.
detail_lines: Roster mode decides lobby assignment sources, not client-side gameplay truth.

entries.title: Tile Palette
compact_lines: Chooses the tile, wall, cliff or object type for painting.
Painting uses the editor data model, not runtime state.
detail_lines: Palette choices preserve hill fields where the terrain catalog marks them visual or object-only.

entries.title: Brush Size
compact_lines: Sets whether the brush paints one tile or a wider square.
Large brushes still apply the same tile rules per field.
detail_lines: Use small brushes for edges and markers; wider brushes are better for surfaces.

entries.title: Height Tool
compact_lines: Raises, lowers or sets terrain height on selected tiles.
Height is terrain truth and roundtrips through map save/load.
detail_lines: This tool changes height_level while preserving surface and object fields where possible.

entries.title: Slope Edge
compact_lines: Marks a height transition as walkable slope.
Use slopes where units should climb between levels.
detail_lines: Gameplay pathfinding treats slope as the allowed height transition.

entries.title: Cliff Edge
compact_lines: Marks a height transition as a hard cliff.
Cliffs block movement across the height step.
detail_lines: Use cliffs for cover and readable barriers; do not rely on them as hidden ramps.

entries.title: Surface Type
compact_lines: Sets ground, road, sand or rock surface behavior.
Surface stays valid on flat ground and hills.
detail_lines: Surface cost and readability remain separate from object height and blocker fields.

entries.title: Objects and Markers
compact_lines: Places object-layer tiles or mission markers.
Objects must keep terrain height and surface data intact.
detail_lines: Markers define mission authoring anchors; object tiles influence visuals, cover or LOS by data.

entries.title: Save Map
compact_lines: Writes the current terrain and mission authoring data.
Use it after validating markers and scenario fields.
detail_lines: Saved maps can later create multiplayer manifests, but consent stays in the lobby.

entries.title: Load Map
compact_lines: Opens an existing map file into the editor.
Unsaved changes require confirmation before replacement.
detail_lines: Load checks preserve authored terrain fields instead of rebuilding gameplay state.

entries.title: Save As
compact_lines: Writes the current map or scenario under a chosen path.
Use it before branching a test map.
detail_lines: A new file path changes editor file identity, not live mission state.

entries.title: Live Test
compact_lines: Prepares the current scenario for a live mission smoke test.
It uses the existing mission test scene.
detail_lines: Playtest export should validate map, markers and enemy setup before handoff.

entries.title: Back From Editor
compact_lines: Reserved for the editor back/return control once that route exists.
Current editor scene has no visible Back button.
detail_lines: TASK_266 records the missing help target so the coverage gate can report it.

entries.title: Command Matrix
compact_lines: Issues the focused fireteam command through existing controllers.
The HUD does not store gameplay truth.
detail_lines: Orders become CommanderCommand and plan data before SimulationRoot applies effects.

entries.title: Selected Fireteam
compact_lines: Shows the fireteam currently receiving orders.
All selects every available friendly fireteam.
detail_lines: Selection changes command focus only; individual NPCs remain FTL-driven.

entries.title: Mission Control
compact_lines: Controls landing zone, dropship and mission-level phase actions.
It mirrors mission state without owning it.
detail_lines: Dropship and LZ choices use existing controller paths and remain separate from help.

entries.title: Move Order
compact_lines: Sends the selected fireteam toward the current target or waypoint.
Movement style still comes from FTL behavior.
detail_lines: Move is useful for repositioning without asking the team to hold ground or take an objective.

entries.title: Defend or Hold
compact_lines: Orders the fireteam to hold and secure the chosen area.
Security and overwatch are resolved by tactical systems.
detail_lines: Use it when you want a team to protect terrain rather than push forward.

entries.title: Hold
compact_lines: Short UI label for the defend behavior.
The team stays anchored instead of advancing.
detail_lines: Hold shares the same gameplay path as the defend command in the current HUD.

entries.title: Flank Order
compact_lines: Asks the fireteam to approach from a better angle.
Leader skill and risk still affect execution.
detail_lines: Flank is a command intent; pathing, cover and timing stay with tactical runtime systems.

entries.title: Take Objective
compact_lines: Orders the selected team to take or occupy the objective area.
Objective truth stays in mission systems.
detail_lines: Use Take when a team should move with purpose toward capture rather than simple movement.

entries.title: Attack Area
compact_lines: Uses the dragged or targeted area as an attack focus.
The area order resolver owns execution.
detail_lines: Attack-area help explains intent only; it does not create contacts or damage.

entries.title: Defend Area
compact_lines: Turns the selected area into a defensive assignment.
Teams spread by tactical and spacing rules.
detail_lines: Area defense uses existing order payloads and keeps map visualization read-only.

entries.title: Area Orders
compact_lines: Drag on the map to create area orders.
Popup choices decide defend, engage, take or flank intent.
detail_lines: Area order visuals help plan commands; SimulationRoot still applies runtime effects.

entries.title: GO and Plan
compact_lines: Executes the selected plan step when mission state allows it.
Preview mode can block live execution.
detail_lines: GO should advance existing plan data, not invent a command outside the controller.

entries.title: Fireteam Stance
compact_lines: Sets cautious, normal or aggressive intent for selected fireteams.
It influences FTL behavior, not direct NPC control.
detail_lines: Stance is synchronized as planning data and later interpreted by behavior resolvers.

entries.title: Advance Style
compact_lines: Shows whether the team rushes, bounds or moves carefully.
Style comes from team behavior and mission context.
detail_lines: The HUD reports the style; FireteamMovementController owns the actual execution.

entries.title: Overwatch
compact_lines: Shows whether members can cover movement or hold a lane.
Overwatch fires only through tactical combat systems.
detail_lines: The help text cannot trigger shots; it only explains the readiness marker.

entries.title: Security Arc
compact_lines: Summarizes the team's current security direction or 360 state.
Security affects flank exposure and overwatch.
detail_lines: FireteamSecurityController resolves the assignments from current command context.

entries.title: Medic Adjacent Rule
compact_lines: Medics must reach an adjacent terrain tile for direct support.
The HUD only reports this rule.
detail_lines: MedicSupportResolver owns target choice, movement approach and cooldowns.

entries.title: Set LZ
compact_lines: Arms landing-zone placement for the mission map.
Clicking the map chooses the LZ through existing controls.
detail_lines: The LZ changes dropship planning only after the controller accepts the placement.

entries.title: Call Dropship
compact_lines: Requests dropship insertion or return if mission state allows it.
Cooldowns and staged units can block the request.
detail_lines: The button calls existing dropship controller paths and does not decide unit presence alone.

entries.title: Dropship Approach
compact_lines: Chooses the approach direction for the dropship route.
It changes presentation and insertion path planning.
detail_lines: Approach direction is command context; air asset risk follows later tactical tasks.

entries.title: Clear Target
compact_lines: Clears the current target selection.
It does not cancel already applied SimulationRoot effects.
detail_lines: Use it before picking a new target or area when the current focus is stale.

entries.title: Fire Rules
compact_lines: Sets game fire permission for the selected fireteam.
This is not a real ROE simulation.
detail_lines: Fire rules are Commander intent. FTL plans read them, but UI does not assign unit truth.

entries.title: Tempo
compact_lines: Chooses cautious, normal, or rapid execution.
Tempo changes FTL plan pacing, not direct unit state.
detail_lines: Cautious favors cover and slower movement. Rapid favors speed and shorter exposure checks.

entries.title: Cautious Tempo
compact_lines: Slower movement with stronger cover preference.
Useful when contact is likely or the route is unclear.
detail_lines: The FTL may choose safer pacing inside the Commander intent.

entries.title: Normal Tempo
compact_lines: Balanced movement speed and cover preference.
This is the default rule set for most orders.
detail_lines: Normal tempo keeps plans readable without forcing slow or risky behavior.

entries.title: Rapid Tempo
compact_lines: Faster movement with lower cover preference.
Conflicting all-round security normalizes to facing.
detail_lines: Use rapid tempo when speed matters more than perfect security.

entries.title: Fire Rule
compact_lines: Sets hold, return, free, or suppress fire behavior.
It is game intent, not real-world ROE.
detail_lines: The rule rides with the plan and is applied by tactical/runtime systems.

entries.title: Hold Fire
compact_lines: Avoids voluntary fire unless a later rule allows it.
Conflicts with assault contact and becomes fix.
detail_lines: Hold fire can still be overridden by future breakout rules if survival requires it.

entries.title: Return Fire
compact_lines: Lets the team answer contact without pushing aggression.
This is the default fire rule.
detail_lines: Return fire is the safest broad rule for most mixed movement and defense plans.

entries.title: Free Fire
compact_lines: Allows active fire when contacts are valid.
Avoid contact normalizes this back to hold.
detail_lines: Free fire is stronger intent and should stay visible in #17.

entries.title: Suppress
compact_lines: Prioritizes pressure on a contact or target area.
Map feedback may show a compact SUPPRESS tag.
detail_lines: Suppress changes plan intent only; combat authority and ammo checks stay elsewhere.

entries.title: Contact Response
compact_lines: Sets avoid, report, fix, assault, or withdraw behavior.
Conflicts are normalized with visible warnings.
detail_lines: This tells the FTL how to react after contact without making UI a combat authority.

entries.title: Cover Priority
compact_lines: Sets low, normal, or high cover preference.
The plan converts it into numeric cover bias.
detail_lines: Cover priority can alter routing and stop choices, but not damage truth.

entries.title: Security Mode
compact_lines: Sets 360, facing, sector, or none-in-transit security.
Rapid tempo cannot keep full 360 security.
detail_lines: Security mode feeds the FTL plan and later overwatch/security systems.

entries.title: Goal Commands
compact_lines: Short #16 actions set what selected fireteams should do.
Move, Take, Defend, Engage, Secure, Recon and Withdraw stay grouped as intent.
detail_lines: These buttons keep using existing command controllers; the hierarchy only labels and gates them.

entries.title: Fireteam Rules
compact_lines: #17 shows tempo, fire rule, contact response, cover and security.
Rules describe selected fireteam intent without becoming unit truth.
detail_lines: Tactical resolvers read plan data and runtime state; the HUD only exposes the active rule layer.

entries.title: Plan Commands
compact_lines: #18 owns plan preview, role status and GO context.
Multi-fireteam plans stay separate from single-team buttons.
detail_lines: Phase planning can be hidden by the fixed HUD, so GO exposes a clear disabled reason.

entries.title: Air and LZ Commands
compact_lines: #18 groups landing zone, dropship call and approach controls.
Air actions cannot crowd the short #16 command matrix.
detail_lines: Later air-threat tasks can add hold, cancel, secure-LZ and evac actions to this group.

entries.title: Breakout Commands
compact_lines: Confirm, Override, Abort and Regroup are reserved for exception handling.
The current HUD reports them disabled until TASK_276 defines behavior.
detail_lines: Breakout commands must answer FTL requests without turning the UI into hidden gameplay authority.

entries.title: Kampagne starten
compact_lines: Einfuehrung mit Pilot und einem Leader; eigener Kampagnenstand.
Fortsetzen laedt den letzten sicheren Basis-Meilenstein.
detail_lines: Neue Kampagne ersetzt einen vorhandenen Stand erst nach Bestaetigung.
Unterbrochene Ausfluege beginnen erneut am letzten Basis-Meilenstein; dein Skirmish-Team bleibt getrennt.

entries.title: Auftrag und Ziel
compact_lines: Satellitenauftrag in der Basis annehmen.
Im Smart Mobile das passende Ziel waehlen.
detail_lines: Erst die bestaetigte Bereitschaft startet den Satellitenschritt.
Ein abgebrochener Einsatz kann wiederholt werden; Anzeigen oder Hilfeklicks erteilen keine Belohnung.

entries.title: Basis und Boarding
compact_lines: Pilot und Leader pruefen; Leader einem Trupp zuordnen.
Ausruestung, Pilot und Boarding fuer den Satellitenflug vorbereiten.
detail_lines: Satellitenauftrag annehmen und das Ziel im Smart Mobile waehlen.
Nur echte Runtime-Bereitschaft schaltet die naechste Etappe frei. Hinweise schliessen veraendert keinen Fortschritt.

entries.title: Landen, Bewegung und GO
compact_lines: Am Satelliten landen und Leader absetzen.
Trupp waehlen, Ziel setzen und GO bestaetigen.
detail_lines: Zum Satelliten gehen und dort Use ausfuehren.
Danach zum Schiff zurueckkehren und heimfliegen. Der Echtzeiteinsatz laeuft waehrend der Hilfe weiter.

entries.title: Interaktion mit Use
compact_lines: Leader zum Satelliten oder Haendler bewegen.
Das passende Objekt waehlen und Use ausfuehren.
detail_lines: Die Interaktion benoetigt die passende Naehe und einen verfuegbaren Trupp. Beachte den sichtbaren Sperrgrund.
Am Satelliten wird die Bergung bestaetigt; beim Haendler oeffnet sich der Handel.

entries.title: Kaufen und Tanken
compact_lines: Handelsposten anfliegen, landen und Haendler mit Use erreichen.
Einen verfuegbaren Gegenstand kaufen und Treibstoff nachfuellen.
detail_lines: Kauf und Tanken muessen erfolgreich bestaetigt sein; nur das Handelsfenster zu oeffnen reicht nicht.
Nach beiden Aktionen zum Schiff und zur Heimatbasis zurueckkehren. Vorgezogene Aktionen ersetzen die aktuelle Aufgabe nicht.

entries.title: Zur Heimatbasis zurueck
compact_lines: Leader und Pilot zum Schiff bringen und Boarding abschliessen.
Heimatbasis als Ziel waehlen und heimfliegen.
detail_lines: Eine bestaetigte Heimkehr schliesst die Etappe ab und speichert einen sicheren Basis-Meilenstein.
Bei Unterbrechung wird dieser konsistente Basisstand geladen. Eine Ergebnisanzeige erteilt keine zweite Belohnung.

entries.title: Einfuehrung abgeschlossen
compact_lines: Beide Rundfluege sind abgeschlossen.
Die vorhandenen Orte bleiben frei besuchbar.
detail_lines: Dein Kampagnenstand bleibt vom Skirmish-Team getrennt. Weitere Kapitel gehoeren noch nicht zu dieser Einfuehrung.
Hilfe erneut oeffnen oder Hinweise ausblenden veraendert keinen Gameplay-Fortschritt.
